content:
Rick Springfield claims he killed a man while touring Vietnam to entertain US troops in the late 1960s.

The Australian musician made the shocking revelation during an appearance on The Joe Rogan Experience podcast this week.

The 'Jessie's Girl' singer said on the show: 'You could tour in wartime Vietnam — it was really crazy. We were there for about four months. I was like: "Great, I'm going to make some money." You know what? Of course I didn't make a penny.'

The tour at one point became less about money and all about survival — when the band came under attack while living with a group of US soldiers.

Springfield said: 'It was like a movie. The call came over the radio, uh, "We've got movement over here, identify friend or foe." They came back and said: "No, no friendlies over there." So they said: "Hey, do you want to drop a few mortars down the tube?" It was a real John Wayne moment, you know. I mean, as a young kid I didn't know what I was doing. I was like: "Yeah, let's shoot."'

Springfield said: 'I dropped the mortars, probably five or six of them, and actually could have blown my own hand off at any moment.' He added: 'They came back the next morning and said one of them hit a Viet Cong.'

Springfield, who was just 18 at the time, says it wasn't until that moment that he realised the gravity of what he had done by dropping the mortars.

He said: 'The hardest part for me was that I dropped a mortar and it hit somebody. It's really one of those things I've carried back and never found a place for.'

When host Joe Rogan asked how long the incident has weighed on him, Springfield replied 'still to this day'.

He said: 'It's hard for me to face the fact that I ended a life, even though it was far away and it was a war and I had nothing to do with it and I didn't really know what I was doing.' He added: 'When I think about the reality of it, it's really heavy.'
